text: Attrition is a gradual wearing down through steady losses rather than one big blow. Here the old Hollywood studios are shrinking bit by bit, shedding jobs and money.
Malaise is a vague, lingering feeling that something is wrong. Here it describes the general gloom over the traditional movie and TV business.
Something impregnable cannot be broken into or defeated, like a castle with walls too strong to storm. The article says YouTube is far ahead but still has weak spots.
A hinterland is the outlying area beyond a city or its main center. Here Burbank is the unglamorous fringe around Hollywood, where YouTube creators actually work.
To gloss over something is to hide or play down an unpleasant fact by treating it lightly. Media giants cover bad news with promises of big hits to come.
Glitzy means flashy, showy and glamorous. The unmarked Smosh studio is deliberately plain, nothing like the glamour of old Hollywood.
A demi-monde is a fringe social world set apart from the respectable mainstream. Here it means the scruffy, little-known community of YouTube creators in Burbank.
Scruffy means untidy and rough-looking. It hints that YouTube creators are scrappy outsiders compared with polished studio executives.
Incumbents are the established players who already hold a position, like big companies in an industry. Here they are the old studios and streamers being challenged by YouTube.
Zeitgeist is a German word meaning the spirit of an era, the ideas and tastes that define a moment. YouTube's films and creators are shaping what everyone is talking about.
Palpable means so strong you can almost feel it, obvious to anyone. YouTube's impact on culture this year has been impossible to miss.
To hone a skill is to sharpen it through practice, like sharpening a blade. Two directors built their craft on YouTube before making big movies.
A blockbuster is a hugely successful movie, one that draws crowds and earns vast sums.
To be the talk of a place means everyone is discussing you. These two YouTube-bred films got the whole movie industry buzzing.
Heft literally means weight, and figuratively it means power or influence. YouTube's money gives it real weight in the entertainment business.
To throw your weight around is to use your power or size to push others about. YouTube's money lets it make moves that challenge older rivals.
Fare usually means the price of a ride, but it also means the kind of thing on offer, like food or entertainment. Here traditional fare means conventional programming such as sports.
An ad-supported service is free or cheaper for viewers because advertisers pay for it by showing ads. YouTube will carry Peacock's ad-supported tier.
Premium here is the name of YouTube's paid subscription tier, where members pay to remove ads and get extras.
Being a hostage to fortune means being at the mercy of events you cannot control, since things might go badly. Studios spend big upfront and cannot know whether a film will succeed.
Bomb has a sense in entertainment: to fail badly. A film that bombs loses all the money spent making it.
To fret is to worry anxiously. Many in Hollywood worry about relying too much on AI.
To dub is to replace a film's spoken language with another. Autodubbing means AI does it automatically, so a video can be heard in many languages.
A fightback is an effort to recover after being pushed onto the defensive. Here it is Hollywood's response to YouTube's rise.
Swipeable means you move to the next item by sliding your finger across the screen, as with short vertical videos.
To eat your words is to admit you were wrong about something you said. Netflix's co-chief once called creators a place for killing time, and now Netflix is paying them.
Killing time means passing time with something unimportant while you wait. Dismissing creators this way meant treating their work as trivial.
Lavish means generous to an extravagant degree. Netflix is paying very large sums in advance for some creator shows.
Poaching originally meant illegally hunting animals on someone else's land. In business, it means luring away another company's people. Studios are hiring YouTube's stars and executives.
Mixed here means some good and some bad. Evidence on whether Hollywood's response is working points both ways.
A mega-merger is the joining of two huge companies into one. Skydance's deal combined Paramount and Warner Bros, along with their streaming services.
To be burdened is to carry a heavy load. The merged studios are weighed down by enormous debt.
To poach is to lure someone away from a rival. Executives say YouTube's creators are being targeted this way, which Neal Mohan calls flattering.
Flattering means showing admiration, and it can also be a calm way to shrug off a threat. YouTube's boss says rivals trying to steal creators is a compliment.
Upstarts are newcomers that challenge established players, often with a hint of cheek. TikTok and Meta are trying to take on YouTube.
A stranglehold is a grip so tight that it chokes off rivals' freedom to act. Netflix broke the grip that broadcasters and cable firms once had.
Creative destruction is the idea that new businesses sweep away older ones while creating something better. Netflix once did this to cable, and now YouTube may do it to Netflix.
A funk is a low mood or a slump. Hastings says the movie industry slumped when TV arrived, until new film-makers revived it.
Raising the bar means setting a higher standard. Hastings says Netflix must push itself to make more gripping shows.
Gripping means so exciting it holds your full attention. Netflix says it must make shows that hold viewers better.
Skydance is the media company that merged with Paramount and Warner Bros; its first earnings report is due this week.
Nielsen is a company that measures what Americans watch on TV and other screens, so its numbers show YouTube's share of viewing.
Smosh is one of YouTube's oldest comedy channels, with more than 45 million followers.
Markiplier is the online name of Mark Fischbach, a YouTuber who turned his self-funded horror film Iron Lung into a box-office hit.
BCG is the Boston Consulting Group, a firm that advises businesses on strategy.
Tubi is a free, ad-supported streaming service owned by Fox Corp.
Reels is Instagram's short-form video feature, which Meta now offers on smart TVs.
